sections.title: The letters ough
paragraphs: The letters -ough make several patterns. The main sound is a vowel heard in (bought) /bɔːt/, which means purchased. A vowel is a sound made with open air. This letter group makes four different sounds in common words. You must learn each word by heart because the spelling does not tell you the sound.

sections.title: Pronouncing each sound
paragraphs: For the first sound, drop your jaw low, pull your tongue back, and circle your lips. For the second sound, glide your tongue from the back of the mouth up while your lips close slightly. For the third sound, raise the back of your tongue high and push your lips forward into a small circle. For the fourth sound, say a short vowel, then touch your lower lip to your upper teeth.

sections.title: Spelling patterns
paragraphs: Before the letter t, this group usually sounds like the vowel in (thought) /θɔːt/. At the end of words like (though) /ðoʊ/, it makes a long gliding sound. In (through) /θruː/, it makes a long high sound. In words like (rough) /rʌf/, it ends with a blowing consonant sound.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not try to find one single rule for this spelling. Learners often mix up (dough) /doʊ/ and (tough) /tʌf/. Memorize the pronunciation of each word when you read it.
